title: Sensex Surges 1,534 Points, Nifty Nears 23,000 as Heavyweights Rally
excerpt: Benchmarks posted their biggest gain in four months on October 15, led by Tech Mahindra, ICICI Bank and Reliance, even as midcaps and smallcaps fell.
body:
• The Sensex closed 1,533.72 points, or 2.11%, higher at 74,315.61 on Thursday, October 15, while the Nifty rose 374.65 points, or 1.66%, to 22,997.35.
  • Tech Mahindra led Nifty gainers, up 4.75%; ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank and Reliance Industries together contributed about half the Nifty's advance.
  • Falling crude prices, Jio Platforms IPO news and buying in Indian IT stocks lifted sentiment, even as midcaps and smallcaps fell.
  • Reader utility: Nifty briefly crossed 23,000 intraday — 23,000-23,100 is now the resistance zone to watch, with 22,800 as near-term support.

Indian benchmark indices posted their biggest single-day gain in four months on Thursday, October 15, as falling crude oil prices, heavyweight banking and energy shares, and renewed buying in information technology stocks drove a broad frontline rally.

The BSE Sensex ended 1,533.72 points, or 2.11 percent, higher at 74,315.61, according to IANS reporting on the close. The NSE Nifty 50 advanced 374.65 points, or 1.66 percent, to settle at 22,997.35, after reclaiming 23,000 during the session.

Heavyweights powered the move

Upstox's market report said the Sensex rose as much as 1,548 points intraday and the Nifty touched a high of 23,056, led by ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, Bharti Airtel, Infosys, Axis Bank and Tata Consultancy Services. Tech Mahindra was the top Nifty gainer, rising 4.75 percent to close at 1,650 rupees.

Other detailed market coverage put ICICI Bank up 3.80 percent, HDFC Bank up 2.27 percent and Reliance Industries up about 3.44 percent, with the three heavyweights together accounting for more than half of the Nifty's points gain. Reliance was also helped by news around the planned Jio Platforms initial public offering, which analysts cited as a sentiment trigger for the stock.

Why sentiment turned

Analysts cited three drivers. First, easing crude oil prices reduced worries about inflation and input costs for India, a large oil importer. Second, the Jio Platforms IPO announcement focused buying on Reliance. Third, a rotation described by analysts as a contra-AI trade — selling crowded technology shares in markets such as South Korea while buying Indian IT companies — supported the sector after HCLTech's better-than-expected earnings earlier in the week.

Eleven of the 15 major NSE sector indices ended higher. The Nifty IT index gained about 1.8 percent, with auto, financial services, private bank, bank, oil and gas and realty indices rising between 0.7 and 1.8 percent. FMCG, media, PSU bank and consumer durables lagged. The rupee firmed about 9 paise to 95.05, supported by a softer dollar index and steadier crude, IANS reported.

"The index reclaimed the crucial 23,000 mark during intraday trade but failed to sustain above it."

— Market analysts, via IANS

A rally with narrow breadth

The headline numbers flattered the wider market. The Nifty Midcap 100 fell about 0.4 percent and the Smallcap 100 dropped 1.31 percent, and overall breadth was negative, with more shares declining than advancing on the NSE. Nestle India, Trent, Adani Enterprises, Shriram Finance and Larsen & Toubro were among the notable laggards.

That split matters for interpreting the session. This was a heavyweight-led recovery after Wednesday's decline, when the Sensex had lost 251.89 points and the Nifty 99.25 points, rather than an across-the-board risk rally.

What to watch next

Traders now see 23,000 to 23,100 as immediate resistance for the Nifty, with a sustained break opening 23,300 to 23,400, and 22,800 as support whose loss could pull the index toward 22,600 to 22,500. Analysts quoted by IANS said sustainability will depend on second-quarter earnings delivering on revenue and margins, broader market participation, evidence of returning foreign flows, and stability in oil prices and the currency.

With Wipro reporting after Thursday's close and large banks due next, earnings — not index momentum alone — will decide whether the 23,000 level becomes support rather than a ceiling.
